items.question: A digits net uses 12 filters of 3 by 3 with padding 1 on 8 by 8 images, then a 2 by 2 max pool and a dense layer to 10 classes. How many parameters has the dense layer?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Count the pooled numbers first.

byKey.no-pool: That reads the 768 numbers before pooling. Pooling leaves 192.

explain.text: Pooling leaves $12 \times 4 \times 4 = 192$ numbers, so the dense layer has $192 \times 10 + 10 = 1{,}930$.

items.question: A confusion row for digit 5 reads $(0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 51, 0, 0, 2, 1)$. What is the per-class accuracy for 5? Give a decimal to 4 places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. The diagonal entry over the row total.

byKey.count: That is the count. Divide by the 55 fives in the row.
byKey.of-all: That divides by all 540 digits. Divide by the row total, 55.

explain.text: The row holds 55 fives and 51 sit on the diagonal: 0.9273.

items.question: A digits CNN is given an image of all zeros. What comes out?

options.text: Ten probabilities summing to 1, set by the biases and $\mathbf{V}$
Ten zeros, because there is no ink in the image
options.why: The biases are not zero, and a softmax always sums to 1.

options.text: An error, because the input has no ink at all
options.why: Zeros are a valid input; the net computes as usual.
Nothing in training taught it that a blank page is a 0.

feedback.correct: The biases carry through to scores; the softmax makes them probabilities.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Follow zeros through the convolution.

explain.text: Each map holds $\max(b_f, 0)$, so the scores come from the biases and $\mathbf{V}$; the softmax still names a class.

items.question: A training split of 1,257 digits is cut into batches of 50. How many Adam steps does one epoch take?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Divide and round up.

byKey.floor: That drops the last 7 digits, which make a short batch.
byKey.decimal: Steps come in whole batches: round up.

explain.text: 25 full batches and one of 7: 26 steps.

items.question: Validation accuracy after epochs 1 to 6 reads 0.950, 0.970, 0.980, 0.975, 0.985, 0.980. Training loss falls every epoch. After which epoch do you keep the weights?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Keep the best validation epoch.

byKey.last: Epoch 6 has the lowest training loss, but validation fell to 0.980.
byKey.first-high: Epoch 3 reached 0.980, but epoch 5 did better.

explain.text: Early stopping keeps the epoch with the best validation accuracy: 0.985 at epoch 5.

items.question: A residual block on 32-channel maps has two 3 by 3 convolutions, 32 channels to 32. How many parameters does it have?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Each filter reads all 32 channels.

byKey.one: That is one convolution; the block has two.
byKey.no-cin: Each filter has a 3 by 3 kernel for all 32 input channels, not one.

items.question: In $y = x + w_2\,\mathrm{ReLU}(w_1 x)$ with $w_1 = 2$, $w_2 = 0.7$ and $x = -1$, what is $\partial y/\partial x$?

feedback.correct: The ReLU is off at $w_1 x = -2$, so $F$ adds nothing: 1.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Check whether the ReLU is on.

byKey.both: That counts $w_2 w_1 = 1.4$, but the ReLU is off at $w_1 x = -2$.

explain.text: With the ReLU off, $\partial F/\partial x = 0$, and the identity path gives 1.

items.question: A row of a feature map reads $(3, 0, 0, 5)$ and is max-pooled in pairs to $(3, 5)$. The map shifts one place right, with a 0 coming in on the left. How many of the two pooled values change?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Shift, then pool again.

byKey.both: The 3 stays inside its window; only the 5 leaves.
byKey.none: The 5 moves out of the row, so its window now holds zeros.

explain.text: The 3 stays in the first window and the 5 falls off the end: 1 of the 2 pooled values changes.

items.question: On the four one-pixel shifts a same-size MLP averages 0.47. What is the smallest mean shifted accuracy a CNN needs to meet the clear-margin rule? Give a decimal to 2 places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Add the rule’s gap to the MLP.

byKey.ratio: That is 10% more than 0.47. The rule is a gap of 0.10.
byKey.clean: That is the held-out bar for unshifted digits.

explain.text: The rule asks for a gap of 0.10: $0.47 + 0.10 = 0.57$.

items.question: A residual block takes 8-channel maps and halves them with stride 2 and 16 filters in $F$. The identity path gets a 1 by 1 convolution with stride 2 and 16 filters. How many parameters does that projection have, with biases?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Each filter reads every input channel.

byKey.no-bias: Add one bias for each of the 16 filters.
byKey.three: A 1 by 1 kernel has one weight for each input channel, not nine.

explain.text: Each of the 16 filters has 8 weights and a bias: $16 \times 9 = 144$.
